analysis:
The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. The supplied patch adds a documentation paragraph at head lines ~980-1027 describing a startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) that runs on loaded EngineV2 slots. It has a greedy 128-token probe pair, solo-prompt and served-width cells, a 20 s wall budget, a retry rule and a rule that no probe or cell trains rates or counters. The supplied base units (lines 1636-2412) are unchanged surrounding text, so I examined them as context only. They describe tool parsers, vision caps, MiMo native ownership, Flint constraints and the coordinator-serving channel. Nothing in them is modified by the diff.

Security relevance of the described warmup: it uses synthetic prompts generated locally, not consumer content (A-001). It does not touch the prefix cache storage in T-041 as described, though the patch excerpt is truncated. I could not see the final sentences, so I cannot confirm whether warmup prompts are excluded from SSD prefix-cache donation. Warmup prompts could create encrypted cache entries or TTFT-oracle signals, but the evidence is insufficient to claim that. The warmup is bounded to 20 s and defers to preemption by foreground work, which addresses availability concerns such as T-029 and T-010.

No code, config, auth, attestation or encryption behavior changed in the supplied evidence. This is a docs-only change, so there is no verified regression. The docs describe source behavior in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, which is not supplied, so that behavior is an unverified contract for integration. The report link target ../reports/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md is also not supplied. Remaining questions are whether the warmup donates to the SSD cache (T-041) and whether the warmup counts toward capacity or routing evidence sent to the coordinator.
